## 🌎 Geopolitics

### Senate passes Russia energy sanctions that could impose 100% tariffs on India, China

The US Senate voted 86-11 on August 7 to pass the "Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026," granting President Trump authority to impose tariffs up to 100 percent on major buyers of Russian oil and gas. India and China are the world's largest purchasers of sanctioned Russian energy. The bill targets Russia's shadow fleet of oil tankers and authorizes steep tariffs on the top five importers of Russian crude and liquefied natural gas to force their energy diversification.

**Why it matters.** India currently sources roughly 2 million barrels daily of Russian crude—a critical hedge against OPEC pricing and supply disruptions. Faced with a 100% US tariff on Russian energy imports, India would either absorb massive incremental costs on its energy bills (cascading into inflation and INR weakness), or pivot imports to OPEC/Middle East suppliers at market rates, both outcomes spiking diesel/fuel costs across the economy. For consulting practices and quant strategies, this opens hedging arbitrage around INR volatility, implied commodity inflation, and India's energy security premium—suddenly, geopolitical risk on the Russia corridor carries real portfolio weight that didn't exist six months ago.

**Action.** Monitor the August energy secretariat guidance from Government of India on import diversification plans. Watch INR/USD forward curves for August-September delivery for capitulation signals. Prop traders should run scenario models on India's energy import elasticity—what % of Russian volumes actually get replaced versus absorbed as margin squeeze in refineries. Check India Energy Dashboard and oil ministry releases for any crisis-response oil reserve drawdown announcements.

### India-China border tensions resurface as Aug 6 diplomatic thaw cracks

The 36th Working Mechanism meeting on India-China Border Affairs convened August 6 in New Delhi, with both sides pledging continued dialogue and agreement to avoid miscalculation. Five days later, on August 11, the Indian government issued a formal statement that any border incident would be considered "serious," following social media reports of a possible military standoff in India's Arunachal Pradesh. Separately, India's Survey of India officially designated 27 geographical features on official maps in contested border zones with standardized nomenclature—a unilateral administrative move China characterized as a threat to border management protocols.

**Why it matters.** The rapid cascade from diplomatic engagement to border standoff rumors to administrative assertion reveals the fragility of India-China detente. For India's geopolitical positioning—crucial for AI talent supply chains, cloud infrastructure localization, and foreign investment sentiment—the border remains a structural tail risk that can flip market sentiment overnight. The naming exercise signals India's confidence but also raises retaliation risk (Chinese tariffs on Indian IT services, semiconductor restrictions, FDI slowdown). Quant models building India-China correlation into regional equity premia just got new volatility.

**Action.** Read India's Ministry of External Affairs statement on the boundary delimitation and China's formal response. Watch for secondary sanctions signals from Beijing—tech sector restrictions, port delays, IP enforcement changes. Track India Vix (volatility index) for correlation with border incident frequency; any sustained uptick signals institutional recognition of geopolitical premium.

*Sources: [globalsecurity.org](https://www.globalsecurity.org/military/library/news/2026/08/mil-260807-india-mea01.htm) · [usnews.com](https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2026-08-07/india-says-talks-with-china-stressed-need-for-border-peace-to-boost-ties) · [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-11/india-warns-border-strains-could-weigh-on-china-relations)*

## 🧠 Artificial Intelligence

### OpenAI's Astra Solves Decade-Old Math Problems, Verified in Lean 4

OpenAI's research-stage multi-agent system, announced August 1, solved ten long-standing open problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science—including the first explicit construction of a non-sofic group, standing unsolved since 1999. The system generated machine-checkable proofs verified in Lean 4, demonstrating that multi-agent reasoning can tackle problems that eluded human mathematicians for decades. The total token cost to find these solutions: approximately $2,000 at OpenAI Sol API rates.

**Why it matters.** This marks a hard capability ceiling break, not marketing polish. Astra's ability to coordinate reasoning across hours or days of parallel exploration—planning, testing, revising—points toward the agentic systems you'll need to deploy for research and engineering work. The Lean verification is critical: it means the proofs are machine-checkable, removing the trust-the-lab problem that plagues "breakthrough" claims. For architects building reasoning chains or multi-hop search systems, this validates the pattern of letting agents iterate internally rather than stopping at single-pass outputs. The $2,000 cost also surfaces the efficiency frontier: frontier models are approaching the point where raw reasoning power, not token volume, dominates the cost/performance tradeoff.

**Action.** Download the 249-page manuscript and Lean 4 certificates from OpenAI's announcement. Read the non-sofic group construction—it's the proof that required the deepest reasoning and best exemplifies where agentic decomposition wins. If you're prototyping multi-step reasoning systems (fact verification chains, proof search, complex planning), Astra's disclosed approach—planning → execute → verify → revise—is the template to implement. Track when Astra ships publicly and what its pricing looks like; if it's under $1 per 1M tokens (Sol pricing), it becomes the default for research workflows.

### DeepSeek V4 Pro Reaches 95% of Claude Fable at 1/46th the Cost

Independent benchmark aggregations released in August 2026 show DeepSeek V4 Pro trails Claude Fable 5 by only 5.3 percentage points across standard tests—or 2.8 points when excluding Humanity's Last Exam without tools. Meanwhile, DeepSeek's pricing sits at $0.435 per million input tokens and $0.87 per million output tokens (with $0.0036 cached), compared to Fable 5's $10 input and $50 output. This 46x cost differential at near-parity performance inverts the frontier model selection logic.

**Why it matters.** This is the commoditization inflection. If you're a consulting practice building customer applications, you hit an architectural decision point: the cheapest frontier-competitive model is now open-weight and Chinese. For engineers tuning inference pipelines, the economic case for fine-tuning DeepSeek on domain data (rather than paying Anthropic's API tax) becomes hard to ignore. For teams building agentic systems that chain dozens of reasoning steps, the per-token math shifts dramatically—96 calls at DeepSeek rates cost what 2 calls cost on Fable. The benchmark parity also matters: Claude's lead has compressed. When models cluster within measurement noise, you optimize for cost, latency, and availability, not marginal capability gains. Expect a wave of DeepSeek deployments in regulated and cost-sensitive verticals where 5% capability loss pays for itself in weeks.

**Action.** Run your production inference load through DeepSeek V4 Pro on a shadow-traffic test. Measure latency, cached-token efficiency, and end-user-visible quality on your domain. If the 5% gap doesn't surface in your application metrics (it won't for most), plan a migration. For model selection in new projects, default to DeepSeek unless you need Anthropic's guardrails, reasoning depth, or multi-modal reasoning that Fable explicitly wins on. Track DeepSeek's next point release—if they close the 2.8% gap further, the cost argument becomes overwhelming.

*Sources: [[DeepSeek vs Claude comparison](https://benchlm.ai/compare/claude-fable-vs-deepseek-v4-pro-0813)]([DeepSeek vs Claude comparison](https://benchlm.ai/compare/claude-fable-vs-deepseek-v4-pro-0813)) · [[Yahoo Finance coverage](https://tech.yahoo.com/ai/claude/articles/china-deepseek-upgrades-v4-pro-200105579.html)]([Yahoo Finance coverage](https://tech.yahoo.com/ai/claude/articles/china-deepseek-upgrades-v4-pro-200105579.html)) · [[Crypt Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/deepseek-v4-pro-upgrade-anthropic-claude-fable/)]([Crypt Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/deepseek-v4-pro-upgrade-anthropic-claude-fable/))*

## 🇮🇳 India

### NVIDIA Leads ₹698 Crore Investment in Sarvam AI, Indian Language Foundation Model Unicorn

Sarvam AI's board approved a $74 million Series B extension round led by NVIDIA, with additional participation from Glade Brook Capital, Gaja Capital, and Indigo Ventures. NVIDIA committed ₹238 crore ($25 million) as the lead investor, while Glade Brook deployed ₹190.3 crore ($20 million). The round values the Bengaluru-based AI startup at $1.51 billion post-money, validating its earlier $234 million Series B that achieved unicorn status in 2026.

**Why it matters.** NVIDIA's direct participation signals GPU and AI infrastructure commitment to India's AI ecosystem. For engineers building language models, reasoning systems, or LLM applications in Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, or other Indian languages, this validates the commercial path: Sarvam's models (Sarvam 105B, 30B, Vision) reduce engineering friction and localization time. The ₹698 crore in fresh capital will likely flow to compute infrastructure, talent, and model training—directly lowering costs and competition intensity for anyone building applied AI on Indian language foundations. This is the strongest public signal so far that tier-1 chip makers view Indian-language AI as both feasible and necessary.

**Action.** Review Sarvam's public model cards on Hugging Face and monitor their enterprise API pricing as a proxy for compute cost trends in India. If you're pitching VCs for AI/fintech plays targeting tier-2/tier-3 India, reference this round as evidence of model-to-product viability. Track whether NVIDIA announces dedicated India AI infrastructure programs in response.

*Sources: [[Silicon India](https://www.siliconindia.com/startup/startup-funding/sarvam-ai-set-to-raise-74-million-in-series-b-extension-led-by-nvidia-nwid-55165.html)]([Silicon India](https://www.siliconindia.com/startup/startup-funding/sarvam-ai-set-to-raise-74-million-in-series-b-extension-led-by-nvidia-nwid-55165.html)) · [[DealStreet Asia](https://www.dealstreetasia.com/stories/sarvam-ai-funding-490931)]([DealStreet Asia](https://www.dealstreetasia.com/stories/sarvam-ai-funding-490931)) · [[Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/companies/start-ups/sarvam-ai-set-to-raise-700-crore-in-nvidia-led-funding-round-126080400522_1.html)]([Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/companies/start-ups/sarvam-ai-set-to-raise-700-crore-in-nvidia-led-funding-round-126080400522_1.html))*

### Zetwerk Files ₹2,600 Crore IPO—Deeptech Manufacturing Platform at ₹15,913 Crore FY26 Revenue

Zetwerk, a B2B contract manufacturing platform, filed updated IPO documents (UDRHP) with SEBI on August 13 for a fresh issue of up to ₹2,600 crore. The Bengaluru startup reported revenue of ₹15,913 crore in FY26 (ended March 2026), a 40.43% year-on-year jump from ₹11,331 crore. Adjusted EBITDA climbed to ₹421.34 crore from ₹322.59 crore. The IPO will also include offer-for-sale shares; promoters account for 53% of the OFS, with a dual listing on BSE and NSE.

**Why it matters.** Zetwerk's path from deeptech startup to ₹2,600 crore IPO validates the manufacturing-tech-to-public-markets playbook in India. The company's 40% revenue growth and ₹421 crore EBITDA profitability make it the blueprint for B2B SaaS founders targeting supply-chain, manufacturing operations, or enterprise automation—domains where India has structural cost advantages and global demand. The IPO use of proceeds (₹1,250 crore debt repayment + acquisitions) signals mature capital discipline, not burn-rate anxiety. For founders in factory automation, ERP, logistics, or manufacturing analytics, this validates investor appetite and exit multiples.

**Action.** Download Zetwerk's UDRHP from SEBI's official portal (sebi.gov.in) and examine revenue mix, gross margins by vertical (aerospace, automotive, semiconductor), and customer concentration risk. Track the IPO timeline for pricing; subscription details often reveal institutional vs. retail demand appetite for deeptech. Cross-reference with recent aerospace/defence funding rounds (e.g., Sigma Advanced Systems' ₹460 crore raise on August 14) to map supply-chain consolidation trends.

## 🇮🇳 Indian Stocks

### ONGC (NSE): -1.5% as Venezuela sanctions approval raises recovery uncertainty

Oil and Natural Gas Corp closed at ₹236.40 on August 16, down 1.5% from ₹239.90, after the US Treasury granted OFAC approval to resume full operations in Venezuela. The license removes sanctions-related barriers ONGC has faced for years, potentially unlocking dormant upstream assets and operatorship opportunities with PDVSA. Trading volume patterns reflect muted sentiment despite the strategic significance of the geopolitical win.

**Why it matters.** The Venezuela approval signals a long-term play for capital recovery from a $5+ billion stranded investment, but the immediate market reaction shows skepticism about timelines and production ramp-ups. For investors tracking India's energy security, this unblocks a key supply source that could cushion crude volatility. Sensex stalwarts like ONGC typically rally on policy wins—the underperformance suggests traders are pricing in execution risk and hedging against near-term crude weakness amid broader macro caution.

**Action.** Investors should monitor ONGC's quarterly commentary on Venezuela capex guidance and production guidance; the RBI's oil-price assumptions for rate calls also matter here. Watch the ₹235-240 support level; a break below indicates sustained foreign selling. NSE disclosure filings will detail operatorship terms once finalized with PDVSA.

*Sources: [[Business Standard - ONGC Venezuela sanctions approval](https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/ongc-gets-us-licence-to-resume-venezuela-operations-eyes-operatorship-126081600145_1.html)]([Business Standard - ONGC Venezuela sanctions approval](https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/ongc-gets-us-licence-to-resume-venezuela-operations-eyes-operatorship-126081600145_1.html)) · [[Zerodha Pulse - Market outlook August 17](https://pulse.zerodha.com/)]([Zerodha Pulse - Market outlook August 17](https://pulse.zerodha.com/))*

### BHARTI AIRTEL (NSE): -0.7% despite Citi 15% upside call on prepaid ARPU unlock

Bharti Airtel fell to ₹1,930.50, down 0.7%, even as the telecom operator announced the discontinuation of five prepaid plans (₹299, ₹319, ₹579, ₹619, ₹649) in a rationalization move. Citi estimated the plan shuffle could lift prepaid-cluster ARPU by 9% to ₹300, driving blended organic ARPU gains of 6-7%. The analyst set a ₹2,230 target, implying 15% upside, but the market repriced higher competition risk and lower upgrade cycles.

**Why it matters.** Airtel's forced migration of budget-tier subscribers to higher-price plans (₹299 → ₹349) represents a monetization lever without formal price hikes—crucial in a three-player duopoly where tariff wars have eroded margins for a decade. If Vodafone Idea and Jio follow suit, the sector could sustainably improve unit economics. For domestic investors, Airtel's discipline signals confidence in subscriber stickiness and suggests management sees pent-up demand elasticity. Sensex-sensitive financials (credit demand, insurance premiums) hinge on consistent telco ARPU gains.

**Action.** Track Airtel's Q2 FY27 commentary on churn rates and prepaid ARPU realization; a miss on the ₹4-12 ARPU guidance would suggest subscriber pushback. NSE announcements will carry competitor responses (Jio tariff moves, Vi operational updates). Resistance at ₹1,980-2,000; a close above ₹2,000 re-confirms the Citi thesis.

*Sources: [[Business Standard - Airtel prepaid restructuring](https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/airtel-prepaid-plan-changes-may-hike-average-revenue-per-user-by-4-12-126081600330_1.html)]([Business Standard - Airtel prepaid restructuring](https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/airtel-prepaid-plan-changes-may-hike-average-revenue-per-user-by-4-12-126081600330_1.html)) · [[TradingView - Citi report August 16](https://www.tradingview.com/news/moneycontrol:c9e678f40094b:0-bharti-airtel-stock-slips-about-1-citi-bullish-as-prepaid-plan-rationalisation-may-boost-arpu-check-upside/)]([TradingView - Citi report August 16](https://www.tradingview.com/news/moneycontrol:c9e678f40094b:0-bharti-airtel-stock-slips-about-1-citi-bullish-as-prepaid-plan-rationalisation-may-boost-arpu-check-upside/)) · [[Business Today - Competitive dynamics](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/bharti-airtel-tweaks-prepaid-pricing-target-price-will-vodafone-idea-jio-follow-suit-548979-2026-08-13)]([Business Today - Competitive dynamics](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/bharti-airtel-tweaks-prepaid-pricing-target-price-will-vodafone-idea-jio-follow-suit-548979-2026-08-13))*

## 💹 Global Stocks

### MU (NASDAQ): +15.0% after blowout Q3 earnings and $50B Q4 guidance

Micron Technology reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $41.46 billion on June 24, crushing consensus estimates of $35.84 billion by 15.6%. The memory chipmaker posted record net income of $28.24 billion and diluted EPS of $24.67, then stunned analysts with fourth-quarter guidance of $50.0 billion (plus or minus $1.0 billion)—Wall Street was modeling $43.58 billion. The stock jumped 15.0% in extended trading, reflecting investor euphoria over memory demand driven by AI infrastructure build-out.

**Why it matters.** Micron's beat exposes the brutal tightness of the global memory market: the company's 2027 capacity is already allocated as AI demand outpaces foundry supply. Revenue more than quadrupled in Q3 as NAND and DRAM shortages persist. For the semiconductor sector, Micron's visibility into 2028 bookings signals sustained capex from hyperscalers and inference chip makers. The stock has rallied 240% year-to-date but remains 20% below its June peak, suggesting institutional rotation into memory plays as alternative entry points emerge amid sector volatility.

**Action.** Read Micron's 8-K and earnings transcript from June 24 filing for the full breakdown of memory market dynamics, gross margin sustainability at 86%, and exposure to customer concentration risk. Monitor Q4 execution against the $50B guide when the company reports fiscal Q4 results. Key support at $966 (Aug 14 level); resistance at the June $1,200 peak.

### AVGO (NASDAQ): -5.5% on August 14 as gross margin guidance signals AI capex moderation concerns

Broadcom shares fell 5.5% to $388.50 on Friday, August 14, as investors digested the chipmaker's flat gross margin guidance of 56% for fiscal Q3 2026 despite record AI chip bookings exceeding $30 billion. The sell-off contradicted Broadcom's projection of $16 billion in AI semiconductor revenue for Q3—a 200%+ year-over-year surge that would represent over half of consolidated revenue of $29.4 billion. BofA simultaneously flagged $370 billion in off-balance-sheet AI financing commitments among chip customers, reigniting concerns about the sustainability of hyperscaler capex.

**Why it matters.** Flat margins in the face of surging AI bookings suggest either aggressive customer pricing or rising manufacturing costs. For the semiconductor complex, the move signals investor skepticism about whether AI-driven demand can sustain its current velocity into 2027. The sell-off drags down the entire custom silicon cohort—Broadcom is the primary beneficiary of AI cluster buildout at major cloud providers. A redeployment of capex budgets or slowdown in training cluster additions could cascade across the memory, foundry, and networking supply chain, pressuring Nvidia, AMD, and ASML.

**Action.** Wait for Broadcom's earnings call on September 2, 2026 after market close for management commentary on customer demand signals and capex trends. The $56% margin guidance is the fulcrum; reaffirmation or cut will set sentiment for the broader semis complex through year-end. Watch the 8-K filings for any customer concentration or booking normalization updates. Key level: $393.55 (mid-range of Aug 16 trading).

## 🏗 Tech & Startups

### Valar Atomics Closes $1 Billion Series B to Mass-Produce Nuclear Reactors for AI Data Centers

Valar Atomics, a three-year-old deeptech company building compact nuclear reactors, raised $1 billion in Series B funding led by Sequoia Capital on August 3, 2026, at a $6 billion post-money valuation. The company simultaneously closed a $200 million credit facility from Erebor Bank and J.P. Morgan, bringing total new capital to $1.2 billion. Investors in the equity round included Apandion, Atreides Management, Conviction, Dream Ventures, Point72, Valor Equity Partners, and others. The company demonstrated a critical milestone: powering an Nvidia AI supercomputer directly from a fission reactor.

**Why it matters.** Valar signals a fundamental sector shift. AI's exponential power demands are creating structural energy deficits that renewables alone cannot solve—and that window is forcing capital into tangible hardware infrastructure, not software abstractions. Sequoia's $1 billion bet says energy-constrained regions will become data-center deserts unless founders solve physics. Factory-manufactured, helium-cooled reactors eliminate land and transmission bottlenecks that plague traditional nuclear. This playbook—finding the unglamorous infrastructure choke point that VC typically ignores, then scaling hard—applies to cooling, water, and supply chains equally.

**Action.** Watch Valar's transition from demonstration to manufacturing at scale. The deal signals 2026 as the year energy pivots from commodity to competitive moat. Track quarterly progress on "Gigasites"—the company's term for clustered reactor fleets. Founders working on industrial decarbonization, water security, or AI training infrastructure should read Valar's build plan for how to compress 40-year nuclear timelines into venture-scale iterations.

### Leap India Files for ₹2,480 Crore IPO as Supply Chain Platform Scales to Liquidity

Leap India, a supply-chain asset pooling and fintech platform, closed a ₹371.3 crore pre-IPO placement on August 4, 2026, led by GIC's subsidiary Gamnat Pte Ltd and Dymon Asia, ahead of its ₹2,480 crore initial public offering. The company priced shares at ₹151–159 in both placements. GIC's participation signals institutional validation from a sovereign wealth fund backing infrastructure for emerging-market logistics. The IPO pairs a ₹480 crore fresh issue with a ₹2,000 crore offer-for-sale—a structure that simultaneously caps founder dilution while injecting capital for expansion.

**Why it matters.** Indian supply-chain startups reaching IPO scale remain rare; Leap's path charts a playbook for infrastructure-as-a-service in emerging markets where asset-light fintech unlocks trapped working capital. Unlike marketplace-driven logistics, Leap pools physical assets—making it defensible and margin-positive at scale. The GIC pre-IPO check means institutions believe the model transcends India; SWF participation in India pre-IPO is typically a dry-run before regional expansion. Founders in Southeast Asia and South Asia building order/cash-flow optimization tools should track this as proof that working capital infrastructure, not delivery speed, is the moat.

**Action.** Founders should read Leap's pre-IPO DRHP filing for exact unit economics and asset utilization metrics—the prospectus will detail what fraction of pooled inventory turns monthly and at what margin. Watch the listing for first-day liquidity and lock-in expiration news; often the IPO structure reveals which founders are signaling exit vs. long-term commitment. Monitor Leap's post-IPO capex plans and geographic expansion roadmap in earnings calls.

### COVID-19 Awakens Dormant Viruses in Nearly Half of Hospitalized Patients, Linked to Long COVID

A Boston Children's Hospital-led study published August 5 in Nature tracked 1,100 hospitalized COVID-19 patients across 15 U.S. biomedical research institutions. Researchers found that nearly 50% experienced reactivation of latent Herpesviridae and Anelloviridae viruses, with 11 separate viruses detected reactivating within the first 40 days of admission. The most common reactivations were Epstein-Barr, herpes simplex 1, cytomegalovirus, and Anelloviridae.

**Why it matters.** The finding rewrites the prevailing model of chronic viral reactivation. The study identified an unexpected mechanism: Epstein-Barr and cytomegalovirus reactivated in response to COVID-19-driven inflammation rather than immune suppression, suggesting different intervention targets. More critically, Anelloviridae reactivation correlated with long-term physical disability and persistent long COVID symptoms—linking viral reactivation to a major unresolved clinical burden affecting millions of post-COVID patients. For therapeutic developers, this opens a direct path to testing whether antivirals or anti-inflammatory strategies can prevent reactivation-associated long COVID sequelae.

**Action.** Read the Nature publication directly. For clinical teams managing COVID-19 hospitalization, the data suggests monitoring for herpesviruses and Anelloviridae markers in patients with high inflammatory profiles, as reactivation timing correlates with severity trajectory. The Anelloviridae-long COVID connection warrants prospective biomarker studies in recovery cohorts to identify which reactivation signatures predict persistent disability.

### CAR-T Therapy Achieves 100% Complete Response in High-Risk Smoldering Multiple Myeloma

The CAR-PRISM phase 2 trial evaluated ciltacabtagene autoleucel (Carvykti), a BCMA-directed CAR-T cell therapy, in 20 patients with high-risk smoldering multiple myeloma (SMM). All 20 patients achieved minimal residual disease (MRD) negativity within two months of infusion, with responses sustained at a median follow-up of 15.3 months. Among evaluable patients with at least six months follow-up, the best overall response rate was 100% complete response, with no high-grade adverse events reported.

**Why it matters.** This result represents a clinical inflection for SMM, a disease historically managed conservatively with observation alone. Smoldering myeloma sits between monoclonal gammopathy and active disease—a high-risk population where early intervention has lacked proven benefit until now. A 100% deep response rate with durable MRD negativity in this cohort suggests CAR-T can shift the risk-benefit calculus, potentially reducing progression to active myeloma and extending disease-free survival. For investors in cellular therapeutics, this expands the addressable market; for health systems, it signals a new standard-of-care option that could reshape SMM management protocols.

**Action.** Hematologists should review the Nature Medicine publication (published April 2026 AACR presentation). Consider identifying SMM patients in your center with high-risk features for CAR-PRISM eligibility. The durability endpoint (15.3-month median) is mid-stage; prospective data on progression-free and overall survival will be critical for reimbursement and clinical adoption.
